data.title: J&J's once-daily pill eases psoriatic arthritis symptoms in late-stage trial
data.description:
Nov 7 (Reuters) - Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) said on Saturday its once-daily pill eased symptoms in more patients with psoriatic arthritis than a placebo in a late-stage trial, potentially supporting expanded use of the drug.

The company said 58% of patients who took icotrokinra, branded as Icotyde, saw a 20% improvement in tender and swollen joint counts, as well as improvements in other measures of disease activity after 16 weeks. That compared with 41% who received a placebo in the 552-patient trial.

Psoriatic arthritis is a long-term inflammatory condition that affects the joints, causing pain, swelling and stiffness.

Icotyde is already FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition causing red, scaly, often itchy patches.

The positive results mark another advance for Icotyde, an oral peptide that Wall Street analysts have tipped as J&J's next blockbuster, with potential to take share from established rivals. The company expects peak sales to top $5 billion across multiple indications.

"Patients don't want to be overtreated, they want a treatment that fits them where they're at," David Lee, Johnson & Johnson's ( JNJ ) global immunology head, told Reuters.

Unlike injectable biologics such as AbbVie's ( ABBV ) Skyrizi and UCB's Bimzelx, Icotyde is an oral treatment, offering a more convenient option if approved.

Lee added that about 30% of patients with psoriasis also have psoriatic arthritis, highlighting a significant unmet need.

The psoriatic arthritis space is highly competitive, with injectable biologics as well as oral treatments, including Sotyktu and Otezla, already on the market.

The trial enrolled adults with active psoriatic arthritis who had not previously been treated with biologic medicines. The company said no new safety concerns were identified.

Patients taking Icotyde also showed improvements in psoriasis skin symptoms. Among those with sufficient skin involvement, 57% had clear or nearly clear skin after 16 weeks, compared with 14% in placebo, the company said.

(Reporting by Padmanabhan Ananthan in Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore)

data.title: Trial failures of Novartis, Novo Nordisk heart drugs leave experts guessing
data.description:
* Pelacarsen cuts Lp(a) 78% but fails to prevent recurrent cardiovascular events in trial of more than 8,300 patients

* About 20% of global population has high Lp(a), and no approved treatments exist

* Novo's ziltivekimab lowers inflammation but misses goal in 6,300-patient heart disease trial

By Julie Steenhuysen

CHICAGO, Nov 7 (Reuters) - An experimental Novartis drug designed to treat a genetic cause of heart disease failed to reduce deaths and non-fatal heart attacks, dashing hopes for the first of several such drugs in clinical trials.

Despite a 78% reduction of the blood particle commonly known as Lp(a), a monthly dose of the Novartis drug, pelacarsen, over nearly five years had no effect in preventing a second heart attack, or reducing the risk of stroke or need for emergency procedures to unblock clogged arteries in the trial of more than 8,300 patients, according to detailed results.

"Everybody in the world, me included, thought that this was going to work," said Dr. Steven Nissen of the Cleveland Clinic, who presented the results on Saturday at the American Heart Association meeting in Chicago.

In September, Novartis and co-developer Ionis Pharmaceuticals ( IONS ) announced that their drug had failed to meet the trial's main goal, but experts and investors were eager for details to see if the treatment had some benefit.

"It didn't do anything. It was completely neutral," Nissen said in an interview.

A second failed study testing a Novo Nordisk drug aimed at reducing heart inflammation presented at the AHA meeting likewise hit the intended target of reducing inflammation, but failed to prevent major adverse cardiovascular events.

Taken together, the findings question some foundational theories about key factors underpinning heart disease.

Currently, there are no treatments for patients with high Lp(a), a genetic risk factor for heart disease estimated to affect roughly 20% of the global population, though few individuals know they have it.

Researchers were hoping lowering Lp(a) would yield similar benefits to drugs like statins that significantly reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes by knocking down levels of LDL, the so-called bad cholesterol.

STUDY DETAILS AND ANALYSIS

Patients were randomized to a monthly 70-milligram dose of pelacarsen or a placebo and followed for a median of 4.7 years.

All patients had a previous major cardiovascular event, such as a heart attack. Other risk factors like high LDL cholesterol and blood pressure were carefully controlled.

Nevertheless, the drug failed to provide any meaningful benefits.

Some 20.6% of patients stopped taking pelacarsen due to adverse effects versus 7.5% among those who received a placebo.

In addition to the study presented on Saturday and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, the team did a separate statistical analysis published in NEJM Evidence. The analysis looked across several measures, including patients who had a higher-than-average reduction in Lp(a) after three months, and only looking at patients who remained in the trial, and it still showed no benefit.

Dr. Donald Lloyd-Jones, a professor of cardiology at Boston University, said in a media briefing that he would not recommend abandoning Lp(a) as a causal risk factor or as a therapeutic target until there is a lot more data in different patient populations.

Pelacarsen belongs to a class of drugs called antisense oligonucleotides, or ASOs, that reduce the production of proteins made by faulty genes.

Other experimental drugs targeting Lp(a), such as Amgen's ( AMGN ) olpasiran and Eli Lilly's ( LLY ) lepodisiran, rely on small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and have been shown to lower Lp(a) levels by around 95%.

Nissen, who is also leading the lepodisiran trial, said there is still strong evidence that Lp(a) is a major cause of heart disease, and suggested differences between pelacarsen and other treatments that may sway the outcome of future trials.

He noted that pelacarsen was tested in people who had already had one major cardiovascular event, while the trials being run by Lilly and Amgen ( AMGN ) include more patients who have never had a heart attack or stroke.

He also said that siRNAs have been shown to be better tolerated and have higher efficacy. "Whether that will translate into better outcomes remains to be seen."

Amgen's ( AMGN ) Phase 3 results are expected in early 2028, while Lilly's are expected in 2029.

TOO LATE TO TREAT?

Dr. Paul Ridker of Harvard's Brigham and Women's Hospital, a pioneer in explaining the link between inflammation and heart disease, on Saturday presented trial results for Novo Nordisk's ziltivekimab, an anti-inflammatory drug designed to neutralize interleukin-6, a key source of inflammation in high-risk heart patients.

The Danish drugmaker, best known for its GLP-1 diabetes and obesity drugs, in July announced that the study, which involved 6,300 patients with heart disease, advanced kidney disease and systemic inflammation, failed to show a benefit.

Although the drug lowered inflammation as intended, it did not translate into reduced risk of death, heart attacks or strokes compared with a placebo.

The news shocked many experts and dimmed Novo's hopes of expanding beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 franchises.

On September 7, Novo ended two other late-stage trials evaluating ziltivekimab in patients with heart failure and inflammation based on the recommendation of an independent data monitoring committee, which concluded the trials were unlikely to succeed.

Ridker raised the possibility that the drug was studied in a population whose disease was too advanced to respond to anti-inflammatory intervention, but said targeting inflammation remains compelling.

Dr. Priscilla Hsue of UCLA, who was not involved in the study, said at the briefing that the ziltivekimab trial involved an incredibly sick population and it was possible that inflammation had already done its harm.

Given similarly disappointing outcomes for these two drugs, Lloyd-Jones said, "It's clear we need further trials using different compounds and different strategies."

(Reporting by Julie Steenhuysen Editing by Bill Berkrot)

data.title: Employers, watchmen at California ports extend contract talks
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 7 (Reuters) - The Los Angeles and Long Beach seaports employer group and the International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 extended their bargaining deadline through November 20, averting a potential strike by about 2% of workers at the busiest US container port complex.

-- The Pacific Maritime Association said on Friday that additional talks were scheduled with the union representing about 250 maritime watchmen at the ports.

-- Local 26 did not immediately return a request for comment.

-- The union watchmen control and inspect truck and employee entries at terminal gates, provide terminal security and guard and track critical cargo crossing the docks.

-- A strike by the ILWU watchmen would disrupt operations at terminals that handle roughly 85% of the cargo at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles, PMA said.

-- The Los Angeles and Long Beach ports each reported all-time cargo volume records for September. Those shipments included retail goods for holiday sales, equipment for AI data center construction and auto parts.

(Reporting by Karen Brettell; Editing by Sergio Non and Tomasz Janowski)

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway accelerates stock buybacks, operating profit falls
data.description:
Nov 7 (Reuters) - Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK/A ) on Saturday reported a lower third-quarter operating profit as insurance underwriting results declined, and said it bought back $9.6 billion of stock in the quarter.

The repurchases are in addition to the $4.8 billion of stock that Berkshire repurchased earlier this year.

Quarterly operating profit fell 6% to $12.71 billion, or about $8,954 per Class A share, from $13.49 billion a year earlier.

Net income fell 28% to $22.11 billion, including unrealized gains and losses on stocks that Omaha, Nebraska-based Berkshire still owns.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

* Jubilant Beverages, which owns the remaining 40%, is not selling shares. No price band was disclosed.

* The company bottles Coca-Cola brands including Thums Up, Sprite and Maaza across 10 Indian states and four federal territories, mainly in southern and western India.

* Reuters reported in July that Coca-Cola had appointed JPMorgan and Citi for a planned 2027 listing. The draft prospectus names six banks managing the offer.

data.title: ROI-US stocks always rise after midterms. Is this time different?: McGeever
data.description:
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.)

By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 7 (Reuters) - The market meltdown following the Republicans' electoral drubbing on Tuesday could signal a rough year ahead for Wall Street. Yet history shows that US stocks typically rise in the year following midterm elections, and usually by quite a bit.

But if US President Donald Trump's second term has taught us anything, it is that many of the economic assumptions and market playbooks that shaped investor thinking for decades may no longer apply.

So as the dust settles on the landmark midterms, the question is: is this time different? Investors' immediate reaction to the Democrats' thumping victory was certainly eye-opening - Wall Street shed $3.2 trillion and US chip stocks plunged 12% in their second-biggest fall on record on Thursday - amid worries that the Democratic-controlled Congress could slow the breakneck buildout of AI data centers.

Is this nervousness a sign of things to come?

THE HISTORICAL PLAYBOOK

If history rhymes, the outlook for the year after a midterm should be positive. In the 12 months after every midterm election since 1950, the S&P 500 has risen, gaining around 15% on average.

But the stock market rises over almost any 12-month period, one might argue. That's true, which makes a deeper dive into the data essential.

Since World War Two, the S&P 500 has risen in calendar years 71% of the time, posting an average gain of just over 9% and a median rise of 11.6%, according to analysts at Deutsche Bank.

So what about the 12 months after a midterm election? Between 1946 and 2022, the market was up 100% of the time after the vote, posting an average gain of 14.4% and a median return of 13.7%. That's a roughly 4- to 5-percentage-point advantage on average and around 2 points at the median.

What accounts for this? Partly, it's because of what typically happens before the midterms. The S&P 500's average rise in midterm election years since 1949 has been only 8.4%, according to Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Wealth Advisory. Uncertainty around the vote, balance-of-power shifts and policy implications builds ahead of the election and can weigh on returns.

After the vote, this uncertainty is, in theory, removed, while divided government and political gridlock reduce the likelihood of major, radical policy changes. Investors typically like that.

Lerner also notes a remarkable curiosity that helps explain the post-midterm outperformance. Since 1950, the US economy has never been in recession during the third year of a presidential term, that is, the calendar year after the midterms.

Lerner calculates that the S&P 500's average return in these years is 20.9%, significantly higher than the average in years one, two, and four across presidential cycles. While there is no single catalyst, stimulative fiscal policy enacted in the first two years often takes time to filter through, while Federal Reserve rate hikes historically just tend not to bite in that window.

CRACKS IN THE PLAYBOOK

Yet no two periods are ever the same, and there are some pretty striking differences between the current economic and market environment and those of midterms past. A few stand out.

First, the stock market has performed strongly in this midterm election year, with the S&P 500 still just 5% below its all-time high even after Thursday's selloff. That means the potential for further strong gains could be limited.

On the flip side, there is still plenty of room for more reversals. Prior to Thursday's market slump, the S&P 500's maximum drawdown this year was only 9%. That's about half the typical maximum pullback of around 18% to 19% in a midterm year, according to JPMorgan ( JPM ).

This is particularly important because the US stock market has never been so concentrated. Whether it's the so-called "Magnificent Seven" group of Big Tech giants, the "hyperscalers" at the heart of the AI revolution, or the dozens of "AI-adjacent" companies involved in the wider buildout, it's a fact that earnings, returns, market capitalization and investment have never revolved around so few companies.

As recent weeks have shown, even if just a handful of tech giants fail to meet the lofty expectations baked into current prices, the benchmark indices may fall sharply.

At the root of this concentration is the biggest investment boom in history. The astronomical sums being plowed into AI, expected to top $10 trillion between 2025 and 2032 by some estimates, have lifted stock prices and household wealth to record levels and, according to many observers, are inflating a huge bubble.

Parallels with the dotcom boom and bust are hard to ignore. The internet transformed the world and spawned many of today's trillion-dollar tech giants, but that journey also included overspending, hubris and "irrational exuberance" that led to the spectacular market crash a quarter of a century ago. Is the AI spending binge, and the mounting debt being raised to fund it, an even greater misallocation of capital?

Finally, there's the interest rate outlook. The Federal Reserve raised rates by a quarter of a percentage point in September, and financial markets are betting it will hike another half percentage point next year, bringing cumulative tightening to 75 basis points. Yet the average tightening cycle since 1954 has been 400 bps and lasted 23 months, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.

In other words, markets are currently positioned for the mildest tightening cycle in Fed history. That's a benign projection, especially with inflation approaching six years above target. While an AI slowdown could weigh on growth, the Fed may also find itself facing the specter of stagflation if conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine keep energy prices elevated.

Either way, Wall Street does not appear prepared for a more aggressive Fed. History offers little comfort here: post-midterm Fed policy shows no consistent playbook, with the central bank having hiked, eased or held rates steady in different cycles.

THE REVERSAL RISK

If the post-midterm pattern holds and the US avoids recession in 2027, investors could be in for a bumper year. But that's far from a certainty.

Recession isn't many people's base case for the coming year, but the turbulence rocking tech stocks right now risks triggering a deeper economic earthquake. Given how pivotal the AI investment boom is to Wall Street and the country's financial well-being, a downturn or sudden reversal could bring the "R-word" into sharp focus.

On the subject of gloomy historical footnotes, the only two exceptions to the post-midterm outperformance pattern in almost a century are 1930 and 1938. The 12 months that followed these years were marked by the Great Depression and the buildup to World War Two.

This time is different, right?

data.title: Environmental groups embrace AI, even as they warn of data center impacts
data.description:
* Environmental groups use AI to track forest fires, count wildlife

* Many say AI's benefits currently outweigh its environmental costs

* Some are experimenting with ways to use AI more responsibly

* UN's COP31 climate summit to highlight tradeoffs of AI use

By Valerie Volcovici

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) - Environmental groups worldwide are using artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife - embracing a technology they also warn is driving a surge in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions.

The contradiction is forcing these organizations to justify their AI use in carrying out missions to combat climate change or protect natural resources.

"We recognize that AI can come with environmental costs, and we need to be thoughtful about how we use it," said Ali Swanson, AI lead at the US nonprofit Conservation International. "But at a time when the climate and biodiversity crises are becoming more urgent, AI can help us move faster and make better use of the information we're collecting."

The group recently started using AI to assess hotspots detected by satellites and send real-time alerts to community forest patrols about potential wildfires in remote and environmentally sensitive parts of Cambodia.

Reuters interviewed 15 major environmental, conservation and development organizations about their AI use. All said they used the technology in some form and expressed concern about the environmental impact of the data centers powering it. The centers, filled with servers, can require vast amounts of electricity, along with water for cooling.

It's a global dilemma for individuals, governments and industries balancing AI's benefits with its enormous risks. The tradeoffs likely will grab attention at the UN's COP31 climate conference this month, when host Turkey will call on governments, businesses and other institutions to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres wants major AI companies to publicly disclose their systems' environmental impacts.

Researchers at the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health estimate the global data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, reaching a size about twice that of Jakarta, the Indonesian megalopolis.

The International Energy Agency, meanwhile, estimates global data centers will consume about 945 terawatt-hours of electricity annually by 2030, producing the equivalent of more than 300 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. That's double current consumption and about equal to Japan's annual electricity use.

The agency also projects that global data center water consumption will increase from about 560 billion liters (147.9 billion gallons) in 2023 to about 1.2 trillion liters (317 billion gallons) annually by 2030.

Technology giants including Microsoft ( MSFT ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google have reported rising emissions linked in part to data center expansion, raising questions about their ability to meet their own long-term climate goals.

Amazon ( AMZN ) told Reuters its artificial-intelligence products were among the most sustainable due to the company's purchases of low-carbon energy and its efforts to use power and water efficiently.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Google didn't respond to requests for comment.

BREAKTHROUGHS ONCE THOUGHT IMPOSSIBLE

Many of the organizations that spoke to Reuters believe AI's benefits currently outweigh its costs because the technology is enabling work that was previously difficult, expensive or impossible.

Kenya's Save the Elephants, a partner of the Wildlife Conservation Network, said it is using machine learning to improve population surveys and study elephant communication.

Frank Pope, the group's chief executive, said an aerial survey of Kenya's largest protected area last year generated roughly 200,000 images that took nine people nine months to review manually. AI models trained on Nvidia's GeForce graphics platforms can now complete similar analyses in hours.

"The results have been eye-opening," Pope said. "We found that human surveys were missing about a third of the elephants, roughly half of zebras and giraffes, and three-quarters of oryx populations."

More accurate wildlife data can help secure financing for conservation, he said.

"Ultimately, these tools make nature measurable and therefore investable," he said. "That's a critical transformation, if we're going to conserve biodiversity at scale."

At the institute founded by the late conservation icon Jane Goodall, researchers are using AI to digitize decades of field notes about chimpanzee behavior in Tanzania's Gombe National Park.

The project was once expected to take 13-15 years because the records were written by hand using the local Kiha language and scientific shorthand.

Thanks to a tool developed with Amazon Web Services, the notes can now be scanned, translated and structured in minutes, slashing the time needed to about two years, said Lilian Pintea, the Jane Goodall Institute's vice president of conservation science.

During her lifetime, Pintea said, Goodall supported the use of AI to advance conservation science, provided people remained firmly in control of how it was used.

"AI technology should be seen as tools which are human-centered," Pintea said.

LIMITING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT

Some organizations are experimenting with ways to limit the environmental impact of their AI use.

The World Resources Institute (WRI), a research group that uses AI to accelerate its climate and environmental analyses, said it limits resource-intensive applications such as generating videos and images, while caching AI query results so identical searches don't need to be reprocessed.

The US-based Nature Conservancy has adopted a similar approach. It uses AI to analyze video captured on commercial fishing vessels for information on how many fish of different species they catch. But instead of uploading huge numbers of videos to centralized data centers, it has installed AI-powered digital cameras to process information aboard the vessels, reducing energy use and data-transfer requirements, said Vienna Saccomanno, a senior scientist at the organization.

"It takes a lot of engineering to make computation on the edge possible," she said. "This was worth it to reduce both our carbon footprint and deliver these sustainability insights."

Greenpeace International said it, too, uses some AI tools, mainly because software platforms it relies upon include AI features.

It's imposing internal guidelines emphasizing transparency, human oversight and "intentional" AI use, the group said. But it would prefer to sidestep the technology due to its environmental impacts and is pushing back hard on the data center buildout.

"While other organizations are asking how to use AI responsibly, Greenpeace is asking whether it's necessary to build all these massive data centers in the first place," said Katrin Xueying Wu, a climate and energy campaigner with the organization.

Other groups now see AI as vital to effective environmental activism.

"It's our job to save the planet. If we can do that more effectively and efficiently with the limited resources we've got by using AI, then we have to seriously engage in that possibility," said Stuart Butchart, chief scientist at UK-based BirdLife International.

"If we don't do it, then we're sort of being derelict in our duty."

(Additonal reporting by Simon Jessop in London and Kate Abnett in Brussels; Editing by Richard Valdmanis and Alexandra Zavis)

data.title: US labor market regains ground as job growth surges, unemployment rate falls to 4.1%
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 6 (Reuters) - US job growth accelerated in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting that the labor market could be strengthening after stumbling in mid-summer and keeping the Federal Reserve on track to raise interest rates in December.

The Labor Department's closely watched employment report on Friday also showed the economy added 84,000 more jobs in August and September than previously reported. The decline in the unemployment rate from 4.2% in September was despite more people piling into the labor force, likely seeking to cushion themselves against higher living costs resulting from the conflict in the Middle East.

The better-than-expected report followed on the heels of data this week showing a rise in job openings in September, which combined with historically low layoffs has raised the specter of the labor market tightening.

"The labor market is heating up across-the-board and supports our view that the Fed will raise the policy rate again in December," said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide.

Nonfarm payrolls jumped by 165,000 jobs last month after an upwardly revised 60,000 gain in September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 65,000 after a previously reported 29,000 increase in September.

Estimates ranged from 35,000 to 125,000 jobs. August's employment gains were revised up to 186,000 from the previously estimated 133,000. Employment growth averaged 137,000 over the last three months compared to an average loss of 45,000 during the same period in 2025. Some economists were skeptical of the labor market's newfound strength.

"Recent improvements in the employment situation largely relate to a major jump in federal government spending in the third quarter, as well as an unprecedented surge in election spending reported to be near $12 billion within a relatively short time frame of August to October," said Brian Bethune, an economics professor at Boston College.

Last month's broad-based increase in payrolls was led by the professional and business services industry, which added 70,000 jobs, well above the average monthly gain of 15,000 over the past 12 months. Those jobs were in professional, scientific and technical services as well as administrative and support, waste management and remediation services.

Healthcare employment increased by 42,000 jobs, mostly at hospitals and home healthcare services. The transportation and warehousing sector added 25,000 positions, the majority of them couriers and messengers, consistent with strong domestic demand.

Manufacturing payrolls rose by 19,000 jobs, spread across computer and electronic products, machinery and primary metals. The increases are likely linked to the artificial intelligence buildout. There were modest job gains in the retail, financial activities and government sectors.

CONSTRUCTION LOSES JOBS

Construction shed 3,000 jobs, the bulk of them residential specialty trade contractors. Residential building construction employment also declined against the backdrop of high mortgage rates, which have depressed homebuilding. Home renovations have also been trending down.

Leisure and hospitality employment dropped by 13,000 positions, concentrated in the accommodation and food services sector. The share of industries reporting growth last month increased to 57.6% from 54.2% in September. The average workweek was unchanged at 34.4 hours.

Financial markets priced in a roughly 80% chance of a rate hike at the US central bank's meeting next month, up from 66.9% on Thursday, CME's FedWatch tool showed.

The Fed last week left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Next Tuesday's consumer inflation report for October could offer more clues on the course of monetary policy in early 2027. Economists are also watching the stock market after a tech-sector rout on Thursday amid fears a Democratic-led Congress could lead to tougher AI regulation.

Stocks on Wall Street were trading higher. The dollar gained versus a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields rose.

Economists estimated the economy needs to create at least 40,000 jobs per month to keep up with growth in the working-age population. The so-called breakeven rate has declined from roughly 150,000 in 2024 because of the smaller labor force as the Trump administration cracks down on immigration.

Household employment, a volatile measure, increased 463,000 in October, outpacing the 421,000 people who entered the labor force. About 1.589 million people have joined the labor force over the past three months, lifting the participation rate to 61.9% from 61.6% in August. But many of them, mostly re-entrees, have not found work.

Young adults have virtually been locked out of the labor market, with AI eliminating some entry-level positions.

The median duration of unemployment jumped to 11.9 weeks, the longest since November 2021, from 11.5 weeks in September. There were more people working part-time for economic reasons last month, with the number increasing 339,000 to 4.840 million.

A broader measure of unemployment, which includes people who want to work but have given up searching and those working part-time because they cannot find full-time ⁠employment, rose to 7.9% from 7.6% in September. Historically low layoffs have anchored the labor market.

Though hiring is picking up, it has lagged economic growth, with gross domestic product increasing at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter. Economists said uncertainty from the US-Israeli war with Iran as well as the impact of AI on staffing needs had left businesses hesitant to increase head count.

"More than a quarter of unemployed workers were searching for six months or longer in October, a share rarely seen outside the aftermath of a recession," said Cory Stahle, senior economist at the Indeed Hiring Lab. "And even when employers do hire, job posting data suggests that they have increasingly tilted their hiring toward experience, leaving people early in their careers with even fewer ways in."

Wage growth maintained its moderate pace, increasing 3.1% in the 12 months through October after advancing 3.2% in September. While that underscored the disinflationary impulse from the labor market, it illustrated the continued erosion of household incomes. Consumer prices rose 3.7% year-on-year in September.

Anger over inflation resulted in President Donald Trump's Republican Party losing control of Congress to Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections.

"The American public will continue to skeptically look at the current economic expansion which is highly skewed towards upper- end households and corporates that are profiting from strong underlying demand and robust non-residential investment," said Joseph Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM.

(Reporting by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama and Andrea Ricci)

data.title: Sensitron Introduces 16-Channel, 270VDC Programmable SSPC Series
data.description:
SPHM/SEHM Series consolidates circuit protection, load switching and real-time monitoring in a single networked COTS module

HAUPPAUGE, N.Y., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sensitron Semiconductor, a U.S.-based manufacturer of high-reliability power electronics, today announced the SPHM/SEHM Series, a family of programmable Solid State Power Controllers (SSPCs) for 270VDC power distribution. Built on a microcontroller-based, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) architecture, the series replaces discrete circuit breakers, solid state relays and system monitors with one intelligent unit that switches, protects and reports on up to 16 electrical loads.

Sensitron Semiconductor programmable 16-Channel Solid State Power Controllers (SSPCs) for 270VDC power distribution.

Flexible, high-capacity power distribution

Each SPHM/SEHM module provides 16 independently controlled high-side channels, each programmable from 1A to 10A, for a total capacity of up to 160A. Channels can be paralleled to drive higher-current loads, letting system designers tailor the power architecture to the platform rather than the other way around.

View the latest specifications at sensitron.com/270Vdc_SSPC.

Protection built in

True I²t protection with thermal memory, instant-trip capability and a trip-free reset circuit safeguard both loads and wiring. Soft turn-on and turn-off limit inrush and reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI).

Visibility at the system level

Integrated current, voltage and temperature sensing delivers readings accurate to within 5% across the full operating temperature range. Measurements and channel status are reported to the system controller over dual CAN or dual RS485 interfaces, enabling remote diagnostics, power budgeting, load shedding and condition-based reconfiguration.

Additional features

  • Start-up and continuous built-in self-test (BIT)

  • Galvanic isolation between the control interface and line power

  • Programmable interface I/O signals

  • Bootloader with field-updatable runtime code

  • Onboard code space for customer-developed application software

  • Conduction cooling with an operating range of −45°C to +100°C

"The introduction of our latest 270VDC Solid State Power Controller represents a significant leap forward in thermal management, effectively reducing junction temperatures by 15% compared to industry standard components."  said Joseph Castaldo, Sensitron's Vice President of Sales and Marketing. "By leveraging advanced wide-bandgap semiconductor materials, Sensitron Semiconductor is empowering engineers to push the boundaries of power distribution in the most demanding aerospace and defense applications."

Configurations and applications

The SPHM Series is supplied as an open-frame card for integration into existing enclosures, while the SEHM Series adds an IP67-rated enclosure for harsh environments. Target applications include military ground vehicles, unmanned and manned aerial vehicles, marine vessels, command and communication centers, energy exploration equipment and off-highway vehicles.

Availability

For configuration options, availability and current specifications, visit www.sensitron.com/270Vdc_SSPC or contact sales@sensitron.com.

Headquartered in New York, Sensitron Semiconductor is a U.S. company that for more than 50 years has delivered high-reliability power semiconductors and power management solutions to military, aerospace, space, medical and other demanding markets.

With over 50 years of experience, Sensitron offers solid state power controllers, motor drives, power modules, rectifiers and transient voltage protection devices. data.title: FDA probes tumour risk tied to Novartis gene therapy
data.description:
ZURICH, Nov 6 (Reuters) - The US Food and Drug Administration said on Friday it was investigating a risk of neoplasia, or tumour formation including malignancy, associated with Novartis' gene therapy Zolgensma.

The Swiss drugmaker earlier in the day disclosed two cases in which tumours in children showed evidence of being linked to its gene therapy drug used to treat patients less than 2 years old with spinal muscular atrophy.

Novartis said that it had received nine reports overall of tumours in patients previously treated with Zolgensma since the therapy was first approved in 2019.

The drugmaker has two separate gene therapies for treating spinal muscular atrophy.

One is Zolgensma, which is administered via intravenous infusion and used for the treatment of paediatric patients less than 2 years old.

The other is Itvisma, administered via intrathecal injection, and used for the treatment of adults and paediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

The FDA said the overall benefits of both Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for their approved uses but that it was evaluating whether regulatory action was appropriate in light of the risk.

The agency said there have been no reported cases of neoplasia following administration of Novartis' Itvisma, which was approved last year to treat patients with a rare muscle disorder.

Zolgensma uses a modified virus to deliver a working copy of a gene into cells. In two of the cases, doctors found evidence that the carrier used in the treatment had inserted its genetic material into the patients' own DNA, the company said.

The findings point to a possible link between tumours and a one-time therapy that Novartis confirmed had been given to more than 6,000 children. They also follow complaints from patient advocates that Novartis was slow to share information about the cases.

The Basel-based firm said it had notified health authorities in a timely and appropriate manner in both cases and that the potential risk of tumours is included in Zolgensma's prescribing information.

Patient advocacy organisation SMA Europe had urged Novartis to provide information on what is known, uncertain and what it could mean for children who had received treatment.

Novartis did not provide details on where the two new cases were in its statement.

The EMA did not immediately respond to a Reuters' request for comment.

(Reporting by Marleen Kaesebier, Bhanvi Satija, and Preetika Parashuraman; Editing by Elaine Hardcastle and Sam Holmes)

data.title: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from SpaceX board
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - SpaceX disclosed on Friday that Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from the rockets-to-AI company's board after more than a decade.

Here are some details:

-- Harrison notified SpaceX of his resignation on November 4, and it took effect immediately

-- The Elon Musk-led company said Harrison's decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the company on matters relating to its operations, policies or practices

-- Harrison, a longtime executive at Google, is currently president of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development. Google parent Alphabet is the ‌largest single institutional holder of SpaceX, according to LSEG data

-- Musk said that Harrison stepped down because there were too many conflicts of interest with Alphabet. "Don has been a great board member. Very much appreciate his contributions," Musk added in a post on X on Friday.

-- Google on Friday reported a small increase in its position in SpaceX to about 555 million shares from 551.2 million earlier

data.title: Tesla to pull the plug on Cybertruck after years of poor sales
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks.

The move is a major retreat from what has been one of Musk's pet projects. In an X post, Musk said the wind-down would let Tesla make more of the Cybercab, a robotaxi he has made central to the automaker's autonomous-vehicle ambitions, but one that has yet to prove itself commercially.

The announcement comes at the end of a bruising week for Musk, as his record political spending of nearly half a billion dollars yielded little in Tuesday's US midterm elections, with the vast majority of the Republican candidates he backed losing their races.

Combined, his companies were on track to lose more than $180 billion in market capitalization for the week.

While it was not immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the specialized components for the heavy, angular model.

In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."

Tesla has been shifting its focus to robotics and autonomy, a transition analysts say comes at the expense of the electric-vehicle business it helped pioneer as Chinese rivals gain ground.

The US EV maker began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. According to automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Around the start of production in 2023, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.

"It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same."

"It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves."

Musk's SpaceX was one of the model's biggest customers last year and bought Cybertrucks worth $131 million from Tesla in 2025 at list price, according to its IPO filing.

'CYBERTRUCK WON'T GO, CAN'T GO'

Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Pickup truck purists mocked its angular design, and safety experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like Europe.

The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to prove that its windows were shatterproof by having metal balls thrown at them - only to leave massive cracks in two of them.

During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future."

But the model has struggled to meet those expectations. Tesla has issued 11 recalls for the Cybertruck since it went on sale in late 2023, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Some vehicles required physical repairs, while others were fixed with over-the-air software updates.

Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pickups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market.

"All of them lost the competition because electric pick ups aren't popular in the US," Munoz said.

But Cybertruck's sharp-edged stainless-steel design limited its prospects in markets like Europe where EVs are more popular. Regulatory approval was impossible for Europe because of rules there concerning pedestrian impact.

"Anywhere where you have crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't go, can't go," former Aston Martin CEO Palmer said.

MUSK'S NEW BET

The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.

Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis.

After years of delays to Musk's self-driving targets, Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. However, the automaker still has to answer the US auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit in September to review the basis for that certification.

"Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill said on X.

However, the Cybercab is unlikely to make up for lost Cybertruck volumes soon. The two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.

About 570 of the more than 1,200 Tesla robotaxis operating in Texas are Cybercabs, with the rest mainly Model Y vehicles, according to the state's Department of Motor Vehicles.

(Reporting by Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Akash Sriram in Bengaluru; Editing by Jochelle Mendonca, Janane Venkatraman, Raju Gopalakrishnan and Jonathan Ananda)

data.title: Daily Roundup of Key US Economic Data for Nov. 6
data.description:
03:14 PM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The October employment report was upbeat, with payroll growth stronger than expected, the unemployment rate lower, and hourly earnings growth faster than in the previous month.

Nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October after a 60,000-job gain in September and a 186,000 increase in August, both revised higher from their previous estimates. Private payrolls rose by 159,000, above expectations and following a 78,000 gain in September.

The preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October, with increases in both consumers' assessment of current conditions and the near-term outlook.

data.title: EMERGING MARKETS-Latam stocks, currencies gain; Mexico peso rebounds after Banxico cut
data.description:
* Analysts cut Argentina's 2026 growth forecast, bump up inflation outlook

* Argentina markets shut for public holiday

* Mexican peso recovers after surprise rate cut triggered losses

* Strong US jobs data revives bets on a Fed rate hike next month

(Updates with late afternoon trading)

By Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur and Avinash P

Nov 6 (Reuters) - Most Latin American stocks and currencies edged higher on Friday, and were poised to wrap up the week on a strong note as investors weighed the US midterm election results, a strong US jobs report and regional central bank policy signals.

MSCI's Latin American currency index was muted, but was set for a second consecutive weekly loss. The regional equities index gained 0.6%, though it was marginally lower for the week and on track to extend its losing run to four straight weeks.

Investors also assessed US Democrats' sweeping victories in the midterm elections on Tuesday, which fueled hopes of a de-escalation in the war with Iran, helping push crude prices sharply lower. But concerns that the new Democratic-controlled Congress could subject AI infrastructure build out to greater scrutiny hit technology shares, while a broader risk-off mood weighed on other markets.

In the region, Mexico's peso rose 0.6%, recovering some losses triggered on Thursday after Banxico, as the country's central bank is also called, unexpectedly cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points. The bank called the move a "one-time adjustment."

Analysts said the peso's turnaround post the rate cut reflected growing optimism that changes to the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) could face greater scrutiny after the U.S. midterm elections, easing concerns about Mexico's trade relationship with its largest export market.

"When it comes to the USMCA trade agreement, it has always been stipulated that any changes or amendments have to pass by Congress. The idea is now that the White House is going to be having tremendous opposition," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex.

"If that's not going to be the case, that's very good news for both of those countries and will translate into protection for the Mexican peso. That development absolutely overshadows the very idea of loose monetary policy."

The peso was on track for modest weekly gains, which would snap an eight-week losing streak driven by uncertainty over US trade talks and dovish minutes from the central bank's policy meeting in September.

Mexican shares were up 0.3%, rising for a third day and heading for a weekly advance.

Separately, stronger-than-expected US jobs report reinforced expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month, with the dollar rising 0.8% against a basket of currencies.

MODEST REBOUND IN BRAZIL

Brazil's real was trading flat against the dollar. The central bank on Wednesday paused its easing cycle, holding rates steady amid a worsening inflation outlook following President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection last month.

Brazil's top lenders have slashed their economic growth forecasts for next year, threatening reelected President Lula's pledge to honor his campaign spending promises while also returning the budget to surplus.

The Bovespa gained 1.2% and was set for a modest weekly rise after a steep selloff last week.

In Argentina, a central bank survey on Thursday showed analysts lowering their 2026 growth forecasts while raising inflation expectations. Local markets were closed for a public holiday.

Chile's peso inched 0.2%, while the country's stock index climbed 0.7%. Consumer prices rose 0.5% in October from the prior month, accelerating from the 0.4% increase in September as fuel costs climbed, though the reading came in below forecasts.

data.title: Four things to note from Friday's US jobs report
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October - 100,000 more than expected by economists - and the unemployment rate ticked down unexpectedly to 4.1% amid a fairly broad-based improvement in the job market.

Here is a look at four notable data points from the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

FOREIGN-BORN WORKERS LEAD GAINS

The US labor force had contracted notably during President Donald Trump's first year back in office, and economists connected the large outflows of foreign-born workers that led the decline to Trump's immigration crackdown. Recently that has been reversing.

The workforce has expanded sharply in the last three months in particular, and all of the net gains in labor force participation and employment -- as measured by the payrolls report's household survey -- have come from foreign-born workers. Employment and participation among native-born workers have fallen since July.

MANUFACTURING COMEBACK

Factory work is another corner of the job market experiencing a U-turn to the upside. In Trump's first year, the manufacturing sector shed 93,000 jobs even as he imposed tariffs on imported goods to try to boost domestic factory employment.

That decline began reversing this year, and since December 2025 the sector has added 101,000 jobs, leading to a net gain of 8,000 factory jobs since Trump returned to the White House.

JOBLESS FOR LONGER

The recent uptick in the pace of hiring has not yet begun to shorten the length of time that people who lose a job are out of work. While layoffs remain subdued and job gains have been sufficient in number to lower the unemployment rate, those with the misfortune of losing a job on average are remaining out of work for longer than any time in the past five years.

Excluding the short-lived surge in unemployment during the COVID-19 pandemic, both the median and average duration of unemployment -- 11.9 weeks and 27.1 weeks, respectively -- are the longest in about a decade.

AI IMPACTS

Most economists agree that the ever-widening adoption of artificial intelligence tools by employers has yet to produce major job displacements across the economy. That doesn't mean they are entirely absent.

"The most AI-exposed sectors, information and finance, continued to struggle and have shed jobs on a trend basis," Michael Pearce, chief US economist at Oxford Economics, noted following the jobs report. "By contrast, professional and business services, which also has high AI adoption, bucked that trend and added 70,000 jobs in October while seeing upward revisions to past months. Those gains were broad, spanning temporary help and management and technical consulting services."

​

(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Andrea Ricci )

data.title: TEN Holdings Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TEN Holdings, Inc. ( XHLD ) , through its subsidiary, Ten Events, Inc., the technology company behind TEN, a Digital Experience Platform that powers the next generation of enterprise digital engagement, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Management Commentary

"Third quarter revenue increased 17.9% year over year to $640,000, as we completed customer engagements that had been initiated in prior periods and added revenue from new customers," said Virgilio Torres, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TEN Holdings. "Our performance reflects continued demand for our digital engagement solutions and our ability to serve both existing and new customers. As we look ahead, our focus remains on expanding recurring revenue, strengthening our technology platform, and accelerating our transition toward a scalable, SaaS-driven business model."

"Our third-quarter results reflect two significant expenses that we consider non-recurring: a $1.8 million write-off of previously capitalized service contracts and approximately $0.5 million in legal expenses. Excluding these items, our underlying selling, general and administrative expenses declined compared to the same period last year, reflecting the progress we have made in improving operational efficiency. Over the past 12 months, we have reduced our annual operating cost structure by approximately $2.5 million through strategic cost reductions, process improvements, and the integration of AI-driven tools to streamline engineering and accelerate product development. With these efficiencies largely implemented and a leaner operating structure in place, we are now shifting our focus toward accelerating revenue growth, expanding customer relationships, and scaling TEN, our new platform."

"We also made significant progress in strengthening our balance sheet, reducing short-term related-party borrowings from $4.6 million at the beginning of the year to approximately $0.1 million as of September 30, 2026. Total liabilities declined by approximately 74%, from $7.7 million at year-end 2025 to $2.0 million, reflecting our continued efforts to simplify our capital structure and improve our financial position."

"One of our most significant milestones this year was the launch of TEN, our next-generation Digital Experience Platform, whose development was accelerated by investments made possible through the proceeds of our June common stock offering, consistent with our previously communicated commitment to product development. TEN represents an important step in our evolution toward a scalable, SaaS-driven business model, bringing together the tools organizations need to create, manage, deliver, and measure digital experiences within a unified platform.

At launch, TEN provides enterprises with a self-service solution for webinars, virtual events, and continuing education programs, with the capacity to support up to 50,000 concurrent attendees. Building on our longstanding relationships with enterprise customers, many of whom rely on our technology for recurring digital engagement initiatives, we see a meaningful opportunity to transition these relationships toward subscription-based arrangements. We believe this approach will deliver greater flexibility and value to our customers while creating a more predictable and recurring revenue stream for TEN Holdings ( XHLD )."

"Looking ahead, we are focused on three priorities: continuing the transition of our business from a managed services provider to a SaaS company, investing in TEN so that it remains competitive, and executing an acquisition strategy aimed at accretive businesses that add revenue and EBITDA, products our sales team can scale, and technology that complements our own. With TEN now in the market, a leaner cost structure, and a simplified balance sheet, we believe TEN Holdings ( XHLD ) is positioned to build a more scalable, recurring revenue business and create long-term value for our shareholders."

Financial Results

  • Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $640,000, a $97,000 or 17.9% increase compared to revenue of $543,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the completion of customer transactions initiated in prior periods, along with revenue contributions from new customers acquired during the current period.
    • Platform usage revenue decreased by $63,000, or 12.8%, to $428,000.
    • Professional and managed services revenue increased by $160,000, or 307.7%, to $212,000.
  • Cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $261,000, a $123,000 or 89.1% increase compared to $138,000 for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to a higher number of on-site events held during the quarter compared to the same period last year. Gross profit was $379,000, compared to $405,000, and gross profit margin was 59.2%, compared to 74.6% in the prior-year period.
  • Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses were $4,113,000, a $1,928,000 or 88.2% increase compared to SG&A expenses of $2,185,000 for the same period last year. The increase was primarily driven by a $1.8 million write-off of previously capitalized service contracts that had been subject to amortization, as well as approximately $0.5 million in legal expenses related to ongoing litigation. Excluding these expenses, SG&A expenses would have decreased by approximately $0.4 million, or approximately 18%, compared to the prior-year period. Third quarter 2026 SG&A also included an approximately $0.3 million reduction in expense resulting from the reversal of previously recognized stock-based compensation associated with forfeited awards.
  • Depreciation and amortization expense decreased to $10,000 from $147,000 in the prior-year period, primarily because the Company's capitalized software was fully impaired during 2025 and no software assets were subject to amortization during the quarter.
  • Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2,000, compared to $59,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a lower outstanding short-term loan balance.
  • Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $3,734,000, or $(0.31) per share, a $1,747,000 or 87.9% increase compared to a net loss of $1,987,000, or $(0.84) per share, for the same period in 2025. The increase in net loss was primarily driven by the higher SG&A expenses described above, including the write-off and legal expenses.
  • Weighted average number of common shares outstanding was 11,999,366 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2,359,622 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Share and per share amounts for prior periods reflect the Company's 1-for-15 reverse stock split, which became effective on December 1, 2025.

Selected Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Results

  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $3.5 million, plus $0.1 million of restricted cash, compared to $1.6 million as of December 31, 2025, and $0.3 million as of September 30, 2025. The increase from year-end was primarily driven by the gross proceeds of the Company's $7.5 million common stock offering, which closed on June 30, 2026, partially offset by cash used in operating activities. Compared to $5.8 million as of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents decreased by $2.3 million, primarily reflecting $2.7 million of cash used in operating activities during the third quarter, partially offset by $0.7 million in proceeds from the exercise of stock options.
  • Short-term loans from related parties declined to $0.1 million as of September 30, 2026, from $4.6 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily reflecting the settlement of $4.6 million of debt through offsetting against a receivable due from a related party, as well as cash repayments. Total liabilities declined to $2.0 million from $7.7 million at December 31, 2025.
  • Net cash used in operating activities was $5.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.0 million during the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to the absence of $4.7 million in advances to related parties made during the prior-year period, partially offset by a $2.9 million decrease in non-cash stock-based compensation expense and the absence of a $1.3 million non-cash loss on extinguishment of debt recognized in the prior-year period.
  • Net cash used in investing activities was zero for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.8 million during the same period of 2025, due to the absence of expenditures for capitalized internal-use software.
  • Net cash provided by financing activities was $7.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $10.1 million during the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower proceeds from the issuance of shares and lower related-party loan proceeds received in the prior-year period, partially offset by lower repayments of related-party loans and $0.7 million in proceeds from the exercise of stock options.

Recent Corporate Highlights

  • During the third quarter, holders exercised stock options to purchase 89,405 shares of common stock, providing the Company with aggregate cash proceeds of approximately $0.73 million.
  • Launched TEN, the Company's new Digital Experience Platform, which combines registration, live production, audience engagement, on-demand content, and continuing education credentialing in a single system, available on a self-service basis or with managed services as an add-on.
  • Appointed Ian M. Lawson as Interim Chief Financial Officer, effective September 30, 2026.
  • Relocated the Company's headquarters to New York, New York.
  • Filed a registration statement on Form S-3 for a $100 million universal shelf.
  • Completed the termination of certain agreements entered into by former management in connection with the Company's initial public offering, as disclosed in the Company's Form 8-K filed on July 24, 2026.

Company Outlook

Mr. Torres added that TEN Holdings ( XHLD ) plans to:

  • Continue transitioning its business from a managed services model to a recurring, subscription-based SaaS model built on TEN, while continuing to offer white-glove managed production services for customers who want them.
  • Expand TEN beyond events and webinars, including AI and automation, integrations, engagement and intent, reporting and analytics, and content studio capabilities.
  • Pursue disciplined acquisitions of accretive businesses that add revenue and EBITDA, products the Company's sales team can scale, and technologies that complement its existing intellectual property, as part of a broader consolidation strategy.

About TEN Holdings, Inc. ( XHLD )

TEN Holdings, Inc. ( XHLD ) is a New York-based technology company focused on developing enterprise software solutions that enable organizations to create, manage, deliver, and measure digital experiences. Through its flagship Digital Experience Platform, TEN, the Company provides technology solutions for enterprise communications, virtual events, webinars, and continuing education, supporting digital experiences with up to 50,000 concurrent attendees.

Building on more than a decade of experience serving Fortune 500 companies, TEN Holdings ( XHLD ) is evolving its platform into a broader, AI-enabled enterprise technology ecosystem. Its product roadmap includes marketing automation, CRM integrations, advanced engagement analytics, AI-powered capabilities, and content management solutions designed to help organizations streamline workflows, strengthen customer engagement, and generate actionable business insights.

The Company's strategy is centered on expanding its SaaS offerings, increasing recurring revenue opportunities, and delivering scalable technology solutions to enterprise customers. Planned capabilities remain subject to ongoing development, and there can be no assurance regarding their timing or availability.

data.title: Update: US Equity Indexes Mixed After Blowout Jobs Report Pushes Treasury Yields Higher
data.description:
04:48 PM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data and company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes closed mixed Friday, while government bond yields jumped after October nonfarm payrolls expanded more than twice as much as forecast, lifting bets for a December interest-rate increase.

The Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.1% to 24,579.43, and the S&P 500 climbed 0.3% to 7,376.86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.5% to 51,285.73. The Nasdaq sank 5.5%, and the Dow plummeted 3.4% on Thursday, following a post-election rout in big tech as investors expect data center buildout to slow after Democrats won both chambers of Congress in midterm elections.

Technology and communication services topped the gainers, while consumer staples and financials led the decliners at Friday's close.

The October employment report showed nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, above the 70,000 increase expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey, while September payrolls were revised to a 60,000 increase and August payrolls were revised to a 186,000 gain, for a net upward revision of 84,000 jobs.

The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% in October from 4.2% in September, compared with no change expected, while the labor force participation rate rose to 61.9% from 61.8%. Hourly earnings jumped 0.4%, above the 0.3% gain expected and the 0.3% increase in September.

"We don't think that the month-to-month swings in the data are what is driving policy decisions," Thomas Simons, Chief US Economist at Jefferies, said in a note. "That being said, this data combined with the longer-term trends in inflation suggest a December hike is almost a lock."

The probability of the Federal Reserve raising the target range for fed funds by 25 basis points stood at 77% for December, compared with 67% a day ago. The remaining likelihood is that the Fed will hold policy for a second consecutive meeting.

The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October, versus expectations for no change in a survey compiled by Bloomberg. Michigan conducted survey interviews over Oct. 20 to Nov. 2, before the midterm elections on Nov. 3. Respondents saw one-year inflation expectations at 4.3%, down from 4.7% in October, while five-year inflation expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5%.

"About 57% (of survey respondents) spontaneously mentioned that their living standards have been eroded by high prices, the highest seen since May and up from 46% in February, just prior to the Iran conflict," Michigan said.

Most US Treasury yields rose, with the two-year up 3.7 basis points to 4.51%. The 10-year yield jumped 2.4 basis points to 4.86%.

Gold futures dropped 0.9% to $4,073.9, and silver futures declined 0.8% to $51.96.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract was little changed at $90.57 per barrel, declining from $102.95 a week ago.

Oil prices have dropped sharply in recent days, with weakness accelerating immediately following the US midterm elections, according to a Macquarie note. "The move appears to reflect the risk of a significant (and lasting) deterioration to Middle East flows is now being priced out."

In company news, Axon Enterprise (AXON) reported Q3 non-GAAP earnings and revenue late Thursday, below analyst expectations. Shares sank 18%, the S&P 500's worst performer.

data.title: Update: Tech-Heavy Nasdaq Rebounds at End of Bruising Week For Wall Street
data.description:
04:48 PM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite notched gains to cap off a volatile week on Wall Street, as traders snapped up battered technology stocks and reacted to a strong jobs report on Friday.

The tech-heavy index rose 1.1% to 24,579.42, a day after it plunged into correction territory. The S&P 500 gained 0.3% to close at 7,376.86, while Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.5% to 51,285.73. Among sectors, tech paced the gainers, while consumer staples posted the biggest decline.

"(Thursday's) technology-led rout wiped nearly $3 trillion off the market value for S&P 500 companies on fears that Democratic control of the US Congress could lead to tougher (artificial intelligence) regulation," D.A. Davidson said in a report Friday.

This week, the Nasdaq shed 3.4%, while the S&P 500 lost 2.7% to log their fourth consecutive weekly losses. The Dow dropped 0.9%, marking its second weekly decline in a row. On Thursday, the indexes erased their gains from a rally on Wednesday following the US midterm elections.

"If stocks rallied on Wednesday because of lower oil prices and prospects of a conclusion to the US-Iran conflict, they dropped on Thursday because of the realization that the growth might slow if the US's 'blue wave' of Democratic victories results in a mandated slowdown in data center," Thierry Wizman, global foreign exchange and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said in a report. "That slowdown in data center construction would lead to a generalized slowdown in the US economy, by extension."

Friday's winners include bellwether Nvidia ( NVDA ) , which rose 2.8%, the best performer on the Dow. Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) jumped 11%, the third-biggest gain on the S&P 500. Micron Technology ( MU ) , Sandisk ( SNDK ) and Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) also rebounded.

In economic news, the US economy added more than double the jobs Wall Street expected, boosting the odds for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month.

"The strong gain in non-farm payrolls, upward revisions to past increases, and the drop in the unemployment rate all underline that labor market conditions are gradually tightening," Oxford Economics Senior US Economist Matthew Martin said in a note e-mailed to MT Newswires. "That frees up the (Fed) to focus on inflation."

New York Fed President John Williams said Friday that inflation has been "too high for too long" and that it was essential to bring it back down to the central bank's 2% target in a timely manner, Reuters reported. Williams said US economic growth has remained resilient amid a stable labor market.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday that the Fed may need to continue raising interest rates to curb inflation.

Treasury yields were higher, with the two-year rate up 3.5 basis points at 4.51% and the 10-year rate rising 2.2 basis points to 4.86%.

West Texas Intermediate edged up 0.1% to $90.60 a barrel in Friday late-afternoon trade, while Brent crude dropped 0.4% to $97.94 a barrel.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) jumped nearly 12%, the second-biggest gainer on the S&P 500, after the vacation rental company reported higher-than-expected third-quarter results late Thursday.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) is poised to sustain "healthy" growth into next year, aided by pricing initiatives and the rollout of its own artificial intelligence agent, B. Riley Securities said in a note e-mailed Friday.

Moderna ( MRNA ) climbed 5.3% as the company raised its full-year revenue growth outlook.

Spot gold dipped 0.5% to $4,065.96 per troy ounce, while silver declined 0.8% to $51.96 per ounce.
