data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX posts weekly gain as metal mining shares rally
data.description:
(Updates at market close)

By Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index rose on Friday, led by technology and metal mining shares, as investors weighed downbeat domestic jobs data that could reduce prospects of further tightening from the Bank of Canada.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 183.82 points, or 0.5%, at 35,789.09, after posting on Thursday its steepest drop in five months. For the week, the index was up 0.5%, after two straight weekly declines.

* Huge Democrat gains in the US midterm elections this week led to investors anticipating increased scrutiny of the AI industry, triggering volatility in technology stocks and safe-haven demand for US Treasuries.

* "What we saw post midterms was US Treasury yields came down, the US dollar weakened. That helped gold rebound," said Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management. "It was a great week for mining."

* The materials sector, which includes metal mining shares, rose 2.6%, lifting its weekly advance to 11.4%.

* Canadian employment fell 4,700 in October and the jobless rate rose to a six-month high of 6.7%. It was the first jobs report since the Bank of Canada's recent move to raise interest rates for the first time in three years.

* "It's a sign that the Canadian economy is not going gangbusters," Cieszynski said. "It's muddling along at best and so they're probably not under as much pressure to raise rates again."

* Technology rose 1.8% as US tech stocks rebounded.

* Energy added 0.2%. US crude oil futures settled 0.3% higher at $90.83 a barrel but were still posting a sharp weekly decline as investors weighed prospects of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

* Industrials were a drag, falling 0.9%, and heavily weighted financials ended 0.2% lower.

* Shares of Trisura Group ( TRRSF ) tumbled 29.9% after the specialty insurer's quarterly results missed estimates.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith in Toronto and Anand Gopal in Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore and Alistair Bell)

data.title: Confluent Medical Technologies Acquires Northern Nitinol, Expanding Advanced Nitinol Rapid Prototyping Capabilities
data.description:
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Confluent Medical Technologies (Confluent), a leading medical device and materials science contract manufacturer specializing in Nitinol and polymer components, today announces the acquisition of Northern Nitinol, a Minnesota-based Nitinol manufacturer recognized for its rapid prototyping and technical expertise. The acquisition further strengthens Confluent's position as one of the industry's most comprehensive Nitinol partners.

By integrating Northern Nitinol's engineering and rapid prototyping capabilities, Confluent further enhances its ability to support customers throughout the product lifecycle, from early-stage prototyping to large-scale production. Additional information about Confluents expanding Nitinol supply chain can be found at Nitinol.com.

"This acquisition represents another important step in our strategy to provide customers with the most comprehensive and reliable Nitinol supply chain in the industry," said Dean Schauer, Chairman, President, and CEO of Confluent Medical Technologies. "We take our slogan of “We are Nitinol” seriously. As the demand for Nitinol-based medical devices continues to grow, we will keep investing in the capabilities and infrastructure needed to support our customers’ success. Adding a Nitinol-focused facility in Minneapolis’ Medical Alley, in addition to our Nitinol Center of Excellence in Fremont, CA, strengthens our ability to help customers innovate faster and scale with confidence."

“Our team has spent the past 11 years building a company recognized for its expertise in Nitinol design, development, and processing,” said Mike Davis, Founder and President of Northern Nitinol. “Joining Confluent Medical allows us to combine our specialized Nitinol capabilities with Confluent's large-scale manufacturing and broad technology portfolio, creating even greater opportunities for our customers and employees.”

This acquisition is the latest in a series of strategic investments supporting Confluent's Nitinol offerings. Recent investments include the launch of the company's Nitinol Wire Center of Excellence in Hyderabad, India, and its investment in industry Nitinol melter, ATI, further strengthening Confluent’s Nitinol supply chain.

In addition to expanding Confluent's technical and prototyping capabilities, Northern Nitinol's Minnesota facility strengthens the company's presence within one of the world's leading medical device innovation hubs. The addition of Northern Nitinol to the Confluent portfolio provides customers with broader access to Nitinol expertise and enhanced development resources to support the next generation of life-changing medical devices.

About Confluent

Confluent Applies Materials Science to MedTech Innovation. Confluent specializes in the expert design, development, and large-scale manufacturing of interventional catheter-based devices and implants. Customers rely on Confluent’s expertise in Nitinol material and components, balloon and complex catheters, high-precision polymer tubing, and implantable textiles. With facilities in Fremont and Orange County, California; Warwick, Rhode Island; Windham, Maine; Austin, Texas; Chattanooga, Tennessee; San Jose, Costa Rica, and Hyderabad, India, Confluent has earned the confidence of the leaders in the medical device community through a proven track record of innovative materials science, engineering, and manufacturing. For more information, visit confluentmedical.com.

Northern Nitinol is a trusted development partner for medical device manufacturers, bringing more than 50 years of expertise in device design, rapid prototyping, and product development. Located in Minnesota's Medical Alley, Northern Nitinol specializes in helping customers solve complex Nitinol challenges through integrated services including design, material sourcing, prototyping, processing, testing, and analysis. Northern Nitinol works alongside OEMs to accelerate innovation and advance products toward commercialization.

data.title: US Equity Markets End Mixed After Unexpectedly Higher Nonfarm Payrolls Report
data.description:
04:31 PM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- US equity indexes were mixed Friday after October nonfarm payrolls expanded more than twice as expected.

* The October employment report showed nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, above the 70,000 increase expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey, while September payrolls were revised to a 60,000 increase and August payrolls were revised to a 186,000 gain, for a net upward revision of 84,000 jobs.

* The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% in October from 4.2% in September, compared with no change expected, while the labor force participation rate rose to 61.9% from 61.8%.

* December West Texas Intermediate crude oil fell $0.04 to $90.48 per barrel, while January Brent crude, the global benchmark, was last seen down $0.41 at $97.88.

* Airbnb ( ABNB ) shares rose roughly 12%, the second best performer on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, after the company reported a stronger-than-expected increase in Q3 earnings and revenue, and unveiled a share buyback authorization.

* Axon Enterprise ( AXON ) shares fell more than 18%, the S&P 500's worst performer, after the company reported Q3 non-GAAP earnings and revenue late Thursday below analyst expectations.
